findings.reason: the plan must name `gs/artifact_resolution.py` and either route the bundle's description store through it or state in §2 why a second env-var-keyed resolver is warranted.
findings.text: §2 makes the engine find a machine's description store by an ordered root search with an environment override (`IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH`), but `resolve_machine_description(cache_directory, digest)` at `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py:344` already resolves a named machine's description by exactly that pattern: environment override first (`CACHE_ENV = "AMBIX_MACHINE_ARTIFACT_CACHE"` line 85, `DIGEST_ENV` line 86, consumed lines 361-380), then the durable cache root, then the node-local staging root — and it is the resolver `gs/machine_selection.py:130` reads through. The plan generalises `resolve_description_store_root` (`machine_map.py:118`) into a second env-var-keyed description-locator without naming this owner, so the repository is left with two environment variables for "point me at another machine's description" and two ordered searches behind them.

findings.reason: the missing citation is the same defect the duplicate_owner finding names; folding the owner into §2's reuse map changes what §2 proposes to build.
findings.text: the reuse census in §2 walks the eight `imas_ambix/data/` modules it moves and their resolvers, but never opens the `imas_ambix/gs/` subsystem, where `artifact_resolution.py` is the repository's existing answer to "find the machine description without being handed a path" and its module docstring (lines 1-60) is a written study of the same problem (ordered search, override, pin). A plan whose whole §2 is a mechanism to locate a machine's maps and description by name cannot be checked as reuse-complete while that file is unread.

findings.reason: §3's stated mechanism (empty `ssh_command`) does not produce the local argv it claims; the plan must add the missing change (split the command, drop the module shell, or a `module_load=False` flag) or its first implementation node will not reproduce the stated done-when.
findings.text: §3 asserts that "with an empty `ssh_command`, `_argv()` composes `nice -n 19 <python> -c REMOTE_SCRIPT` as a list: no ssh prefix and no module shell". Opening the code, `_remote_shell_command()` (`eddb_remote.py:305-320`) unconditionally returns the string `"module unload python/3.5.6; module load python/3.12; nice -n 19 python -c '<script>'"`, and `_argv()` (`eddb_remote.py:322-327`) returns `[*prefix, that_string]` — a **one-element list holding a shell string**, not `[nice, -n, 19, ...]`. `SshTransport.run` (`eddb_remote.py:166-184`) execs that argv with `subprocess.run(...)` and no `shell=True`, so an empty `ssh_command` yields a single argument that is not an executable path and raises `FileNotFoundError` (surfaced as `EddbRemoteError`). The module shell is the *remote* command ssh runs through the server's login shell; locally there is no shell to run it, so the seam as the plan describes it is not reachable without also changing `_remote_shell_command`.

findings.reason: the plan's blast radius is under-counted; the direct-constant sites and the staying `nova.io.cocos` importers must be enumerated so the move node budgets for them instead of discovering them at the gate.
findings.text: §2 retires the module-level packaged roots ("Those two retire the module-level packaged roots and the `getattr` lookup", §2) yet also says the roots stay with ambix, and it asserts "Every call site of the by-name loaders changes only its import". At least five call sites never go through the by-name loaders and dereference the constants directly, so they do not move with an import-only change: `imas_ambix/spine_bench/transform_geometry_source.py:31` (imports `PACKAGED_MACHINE_MAP_ROOT`) and `:362` (reads `PACKAGED_MACHINE_MAP_ROOT / "mast.json"`); `tests/data/test_jt60sa_signal_maps.py:24` (import) and `:38` (`UNIT_TABLE_PATH = PACKAGED_MACHINE_MAP_ROOT / "jt-60sa-eddb-units.json"`); `tests/data/test_machine_map.py:24` (imports `LINKML_SCHEMA_PATH`) with `:202`, `:1704`, `:1724` reading `LINKML_SCHEMA_PATH.parent / "mast.json"`. In the same family, the §2 edit set omits the ambix-side `nova.io.cocos` importers that stay in the tree while `nova` drops the re-export: `imas_ambix/data/cocos_convention.py:26` (`CONVENTION_DIGITS`), `imas_ambix/challenge/convention.py:28` (`convention`) and `tests/data/test_cocos_convention.py:11` (`transform_factor`) — the plan names only `imas_ambix/cocos.py:20`.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the engine (`imas_alambic`) hides the loader/transport/cocos surface behind a small import face, and §2 generalises three existing resolvers in place rather than spreading them.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan adds `IMAS_ALAMBIC_MAP_PATH` plus an ordered bundle search as a second by-name machine resolver with an environment override, while `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py` already owns that mechanism (`AMBIX_MACHINE_ARTIFACT_CACHE`/`AMBIX_MACHINE_ARTIFACT_DIGEST`).
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2's own "interface account" names the retirement of the module-level packaged roots and (with §6) of `imas-ambix data mint`, and states why the environment variable and entry-point group are needed, so no section adds surface unaccounted for.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan's reuse map covers only the `imas_ambix/data/` modules it moves and never opens `imas_ambix/gs/artifact_resolution.py`, which already owns by-name, env-override-first machine-description resolution; §3's account of the `eddb_remote.py` seam is also contradicted by the code.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 states why the by-name loaders are generalised rather than wrapped ("generalises those three in place … rather than adding a resolver beside them") and §3 states why no second `Transport` class is added.
